function X(m) { return X0 + m * SX; }
function Y(z) { return Y0 - z * SZ; }
function r1(v) { return Math.round(v * 10) / 10; }
function clamp(v, a, b) { return Math.max(a, Math.min(b, v)); }
function path(pts, close) {
  var s = '';
  for (var i = 0; i < pts.length; i++)
    s += (i ? ' L' : 'M') + r1(X(pts[i][0])) + ',' + r1(Y(pts[i][1]));
  return s + (close ? ' Z' : '');
}
function basePts(e) {
  var pts = [[XSTART, ZTOP], [e, ZTOP]], i;
  for (i = 1; i < CLIFF.length; i++)
    pts.push([e + CLIFF[i][0], CLIFF[i][1]]);
  for (i = 1; i < BEACH.length; i++)
    pts.push([e + BEACH[i][0], BEACH[i][1]]);
  pts.push([XEND, SEABED_END]);
  return pts;
}

function surveyPts(h, w, n) {
  var top = sandTop(h, w), x0 = top[0][0] + 3,
      x1 = top[top.length - 1][0] - 3, out = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    var x = x0 + i * (x1 - x0) / (n - 1);
    out.push([x, pointOn(top, x)]);
  }
  return out;
}

From a company name
to a meaningful action.

The skill guides your AI agent through research, concept development, a working scene, and a critique. You approve the direction before it builds.

Find the story

Find the message behind the company.

The agent researches public official sources and recommends what visitors should understand. You confirm the brief before concepts begin.

You bring
A company or product name, plus any audience or takeaway you already have.
The agent does
Checks official pages, claims, asset URLs, and reuse constraints. Flags any missing evidence for your review.

Shape the interaction

Choose a visitor action that carries the story.

Review four concepts with visual previews. Each connects an action, a visible consequence, and the company message.

You choose
The direction that fits your story. Reference screenshots can help explain the visuals you expect.
The agent does
Shows the proposed composition, main interaction, and takeaway before building. Your approved choices carry into the next stage.

Prove a working scene

Make the visitor's action
change something meaningful.

The agent builds a representative scene with permitted official assets, then checks the input, visible response, and explanation together.

You review
Whether the action and response communicate the intended story clearly.
The agent does
Extends the working scene into the experience, including keyboard and touch access, English/Dutch, Sources, and Download HTML.

Inspect, then take the HTML

Refine your approved experience.

The agent critiques the opening, interaction, and takeaway, then replays affected states. Revisions preserve your approved concept and assets.

You receive
One online-first HTML file. Internet access is required for external assets; visitors do not need the skill.
Need offline delivery?
Ask explicitly. The agent attempts permitted downloads and embedding, then verifies a network-blocked replay or reports the limitation.

Choose a stage to see your part and the agent's part in this workflow guide.

The skill is the authoring guidance. The HTML is what your audience uses.

Visitors need a compatible browser, not the skill or an AI agent. The default output uses official online asset URLs and is labelled "Online version - internet required for external assets". A Download HTML button does not make it offline.

Visual direction, critique, polish, and 30 curated interaction patterns are bundled. No separate design-skill installation is needed.

Install once.
Bring your next story.

Choose the instructions for your authoring environment. Installation support depends on that agent's skill-loading capabilities.

Public source and skill downloads

Browse the source and download the skill from the public GitHub repository. You do not need a GitHub account to download the files.

Cowork

Import the packaged skill.

  1. Open the .skill file on GitHub.
  2. Choose Download raw file and save interactive-experience-generator.skill.
  3. Import that file into Cowork using its skill import controls. Re-import after updates.
  4. Start a task with one of the prompts below.
Get Cowork skill on GitHub

Public download. This opens the file page, not an installer.

Other agents

Keep the complete skill folder together.

  1. Get the files from the public source repository.
  2. Create an interactive-experience-generator folder in your agent's documented skill location.
  3. Copy these items into it, preserving their directory structure:
interactive-experience-generator/
  SKILL.md
  references/
  NOTICE.md
  licenses/
  scripts/

SKILL.md alone is not enough. Follow your agent's loading instructions. Support is not universal.

Read repository instructions

A company name
is enough to begin.

Use a starting prompt in your agent after installing the skill. These are example requests, not prebuilt demos or promised results.

Optional: attach reference images or screenshots of the visuals you want. They help the agent understand your expectations. Use references for direction; reuse only assets you have permission to use.

Start with a company

Use interactive-experience-generator to create an interactive experience for [company name]. Research official sources and recommend a company message and concept before building.

Bring a product and an action

Use interactive-experience-generator for [company and product]. I want visitors to [action] and understand [takeaway]. Research public official sources, use permitted official asset URLs, and keep the result usable with touch and keyboard.

Refine an existing experience

Use interactive-experience-generator to refine the attached HTML. Keep the approved concept, assets, and visitor input. Improve [specific issue], then check the opening, interaction, and takeaway.

Before you build

Online-first is the default. Research and authoring need an equipped AI agent; visitors need internet access for external assets.

Your authoring environment needs

  • A skill-capable agent with file output and HTML preview.
  • Public official-source research and discovery of permitted logo and image URLs. Local downloads are not a prerequisite.
  • A browser to inspect visuals and interactions in the declared delivery mode.
  • Your review of company claims, permissions, and the final experience.

Keep these boundaries in mind

  • Research and brand assets must be publicly available, not private or internal. Public access does not grant reuse rights.
  • The skill cannot add tools, bypass website restrictions, or guarantee every asset will load. A missing usable official asset needs a specific approved substitute.
  • 3D scenes need a compatible browser and graphics support; device performance varies.
  • Check your agent's privacy and data policies before sharing material.
Is this a hosted generator or an AI subscription?

It is a set of instructions and bundled references for your AI agent. This page does not run an AI service or provide an agent subscription. Your agent's availability, costs, and tool limits apply.

Can I use the finished HTML without installing the skill?

Yes. The skill is for making and revising the experience. Visitors open its HTML in a compatible browser. By default, the file loads official assets online and requires internet access. This showcase is separate: its supplied gallery demos have embedded assets; they do not define the delivery mode of new builds.

Can I ask for an offline version?

Yes. Explicitly request an offline or self-contained export. The agent attempts permitted asset downloads, embeds dependencies, and checks a network-blocked replay. If that cannot be verified, it keeps the working online version and reports the limitation. Download HTML alone saves the declared online version, not an offline export.

Do these examples mean every output will look like them?

No. The Heineken and Haskoning files are supplied examples, preserved as received. Their illustrative staging and existing notes are not a guarantee of current skill compliance or future output quality. New work follows the current skill guidance and the specific approved brief, including its required demonstration disclaimer.

What should I share with the agent?

A company name can start the research. Add your intended audience, desired takeaway, and constraints when you have them. Reference images or screenshots of your desired visuals are optional and help explain your expectations; they do not grant rights to reuse the pictured assets. Use public references and publicly available brand assets, not confidential or internal material. Uploads are not required to start.

Where do the product claims and installation steps come from?

This page summarizes the repository's public README and SKILL.md. The online-first workflow and installation instructions were checked for this repository showcase on 13 November 2026. Follow those files for current requirements and reference-library updates. Each supplied demo has its own Sources panel; publication does not certify its claims, asset permissions, or compliance with the latest skill.
